chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Kept by a woman: apartment, pistol, tailored suits and a gold horn
summary: She moved him into an apartment with a sunken tub, gave him a pearl-handled automatic and suits, and he recovered his own horn from Blunt, as the Depression arrived.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: I took a second look and forgot all about Mr. Blunt into the love action. I said I need to go to school now. So I went down and went in. So she said, well, yes. You need an apartment. Well, everybody was living (inaudible) apartments, had those sunken bathtubs at that time, that was something else. Sunken bathtubs and mosaic floors and mosaic in the bathroom. And she said, "Well, I'm going to get you that and you won't have to worry about those Jeff Blunt or anyone else." And I said, well, why not.

So I moved down. But she would be away about three or four days. "Oh, I had to go downtown to see my folks and everything. And by the way, if you need this..." and give me a pearl handle automatic. "Because you're not big and your hands ain't big for fighting people." I said, "They're not." Because what I knew about them firearms, because one uncle I had, Uncle Willy, he had a colt, one of the longest colts I ever seen. And he wore it day and night. And he slept with this colt. And one night while he was sleeping, I had my mind to buy a .22. And I got to his money belt and took $10.00 out of there. And the next day he didn't say nothing, But he told me this, he says, "Sonny, if you see that
person that took that $10.00 out of Uncle's bag, his belt, you tell him to put it right back in there and I will not tell his mother anything." I said, "I sure will, Uncle. I sure will."

I haven't heard a word since -- that's -- the man has never spoken about 20 or 25 words since -- So I knew about those fire-arms. And so I got this firearm and now I'm getting all this money in my pocket, and getting these new suits, and that time having teddy bear coats. And I was getting hats made. Sam Stein was making hats, had another man, his name was Schwartz & Harrison, they were making those beautiful suits, camel hair coats, Florsheim shoes, oh, la, la.

And then I said, I think we'd better go up there and get my horn. She said, well, you've got a gold horn now. I said, yes, but I want that one, too. So I come -- I walks in and I'm a man, now. I walks in, he says, "Hello, boy." said, will you ask Mr. Blunt to give me my horn. I'd like to ask him something for five minutes (inaudible). He was pouring over that chick. (Inaudible). He said, you were too young, that is why. I said, too young for what? (Laughter.)

So anyway, he gives me my horn. He said, do you "Do you want to play?" I said, "No, Mr. Clifford." want to play? I said, no, Mr. Jackson said, I was resting, feeling good, (inaudible). Had my first taste of cavier.
